package.name: Test
package.author: Peersus contributors
package.description: A page that tries the extension contract in context: controls and their results together, editable status, notifications, and deliberately misbehaving buttons behind a setting.
package.changelog: 0.1.3: status label can be defined, changed, hidden and reset with its result shown in place; touch drawing sits beside its pad, added rows stay by their button, and cross-page buttons were removed. 0.1.2: every button asks the application through its contract and shows the answer; every element, colour and event of a page; the misbehaving buttons behind a setting.

exports.description: What the Test page shows, and what a person does on it.

event.description: Answers what a person did on the Test page with the page as it is after it.

bump.description: Counts one run of one of its key-bindable actions; the Test page shows the count.

notify.description: Asks the application for a notification inside the window, as the page's Say something does.

question.description: Asks the application for a question that also reaches outside the window, as the page's Ask a question does.

actions.label: Count a key press
actions.help: Adds one to the count of key presses on the Test page.

actions.label: Count, with a long description
actions.help: Adds one to the count on the Test page, like the first, and carries a description long enough to show how a long one scrolls inside its own short box on the Binds page instead of making its row tall; at most 280 characters are accepted.

actions.label: Say something in the window
actions.help: Shows a notification inside the window only, as the page's Say something does. Needs the notification permission.

actions.label: Ask a question outside the window
actions.help: Shows a question with two answers that also reaches outside the window (the system's notifications), as the page's Ask a question does. Needs the notification permission.

settings.label: Add Test to page
settings.help: Also show Test as its own page; keep the original Test in these settings.

settings.label: Show the misbehaving buttons
settings.help: Show the buttons that make Test misbehave on purpose (flood, nonsense, never answer, spin, fill memory, leave), each with what the application should do.

pages.title: What this extension does
pages.explains: Test draws controls and their feedback together. Its page can show settings, language, system, allowed peers and extensions; you can type a custom status label (Testing by default), show or hide it, and request notifications. Misbehaving buttons remain behind a setting.
pages.changes: Installing adds the Test page. A status you turn on is sent to paired devices and shown on their Devices pages until you turn it off or the extension stops; changing its label while it is on changes what they see. Notifications appear in the app, or via the system while it is in the background if permitted. Other probes need their own permissions. No Test page button adds a Settings page or hides an action. Removing Test removes its page and status.
